Controlled TfOH- or AuCl-catalyzed cycloisomerization and 
tandem hydrolytic defluorination of 1,2-allenyl perfluoroalkyl 
ketones  
Can Xue,[a] Xin Huang,[a] Shangze Wu,[a] Chunling Fu,*[a] and Shengming Ma*[a] 
An efficient TfOH- or AuCl-catalyzed cycloisomerization reaction of easily available n-perfluoroalkyl 1,2-allenyl ketones 
occurring smoothly to form 2-perfluoroalkylfurans has been reported. In the presence of TfOH and H2O, corresponding 
tandem hydrolytic defluorination afforded multi-substituted furan-2-yl n-perfluoroalkyl ketones.       
Introduction 
As one of the ubiquitous heterocyclic cores, furan plays a 
significant role in organic synthesis, 1 and also br oadly exist in 
natural products2 and useful materials. 3 Many efforts have 
been made to construct intricacy furan derivatives, 4-10 among 
which transition metal -catalyzed (such as Ag, Au, Pd, Rh, etc.) 
cycloisomerization of allenones 6-10 (a, Scheme 1) came o ut to 
be more apposite due to the substituent -loading capability of 
the unique substrates. On the other hand, due to the extensive 
application in the field of functional materials and the 
importance of organofluorine compounds, 11 the development 
of synthet ic methodologies for generating perfluoroalkyl 
substituted heterocycles are of current interest. In our 
previous work, we have reported a TfOH-catalyzed12 direct 
formation of furanyl perfluoroalkyl ketones  from easily 
available n-perfluoroalkyl allenones 13 (b, Scheme 1). 14 In this 
study, we wish  to describe the TfOH- or AuCl -catalyzed 
controlled cycloisomerization of perfluoroalkyl allenones  
affording perfluoroalkyl furans first, which may be converted  
to the  corresponding hydrolytic defluorina tion ketones  in the 
presence of TfOH and water. 
 
Scheme 1. Cyclization reactions of ordinary allenones  and perfluoroalkyl 
allenones. 
Results and Discussion 
We started to explore the cycloisomerization reaction with 
fully-substituted pe rfluoroalkyl allenone 1a as the model 
substrate. No reaction occurred when AuCl was used as the 
catalyst (entry 1, Table 1), while AuCl 3 produced perfluoroalkyl 
furan 2a in only 46% NMR yield (entry 2, Table 1). It is 
interesting for us to observe that age d triflic acid could 
catalyze the conversion of perfluoroalkyl substituted allenone 
1a to form furan 2a together with furanyl ketone 3a (entry 3, 
Table 1). To our delight, furan 2a was formed in 96% NMR 
yield as the sole product (entry 5, Table 1) with a c atalytic 
amount of newly purchased TfOH (5 mol%) in toluene at 60 oC 
for 10 h.

Conclusions 
In conclusio n, we have developed an efficient controlled 
cycloisomerization of allenyl perfluoroalkyl ketones under the 
catalysis of AuCl (for 3 -monoaryl allenones) or TfOH (for fully -
substituted allenones) to afford 2 -perfluoroalkyl furans. In the 
presence of water a nd a catalytic amount of TfOH, these 
furans would be efficiently transformed into corresponding 
furan-2-yl perfluoroalkyl ketones. Further studies in this area 
are still undergoing in our laboratory.

Experimental Section 
General：Perfluoroalkyl allenones were prepared according to 
the literature procedures. 13 Toluene was distilled from Na 
wire/ benzophenone. TfOH (Alfa) was stored in a glovebox, 
and transferred with a microsyringe. Other commercially 
available chemicals were purch ased and used without 
additional purification. The reactions were performed under 
an atmosphere of nitrogen using standard Schlenk tubes 
unless otherwise. Petroleum ether with a boiling point ranges 
from 30 to 60 oC was used. Flash -column chromatography wa s 
carried out on silica gel H (10 –40 μ). 1H NMR spectra (300 
MHz) were recorded using TMS as an internal standard (δ 0 
ppm). 13C NMR spectra (75 MHz) were recorded using CDCl 3 as 
an internal standard (δ 77.00 ppm). 19F NMR spectra (282 
MHz) were recorded u sing CFCl 3 as an internal standard (δ 0 
ppm). IR spectra were recorded with a Perkin -Elmer 983G 
instrument. Mass spectrometry was taken with an HP 5989A 
system. High -resolution mass spectrometry was determined 
with a Finnigan MAT 8430 or Bruker APEXIII ins trument. The 
structure of 2d, 2e, 2g, 2k, and 2l were established by the NOE 
study.
